title: Moroni introduces the account
summary: Moroni explains that his account comes from the twenty-four plates found by Limhi’s people, and that he gives only part of the record, from the tower until the people’s destruction.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says he is giving an account of ancient inhabitants destroyed by the Lord in the north country.
Moroni says his account comes from the twenty-four plates found by the people of Limhi, called the Book of Ether.
Moroni says the record includes material about creation, Adam, and events up to the tower, but he does not write those things here.
Moroni says he gives part of the account, from the tower until the people were destroyed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Moroni can be shown as a present-day narrator presenting the record.
unspecified_visual_details: Moroni’s appearance, clothing, location, and the plates’ appearance are not stated.

narration.text: I, Moroni, proceed to give an account
from the tower down until they were destroyed.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni is the narrator; the chapter begins with record-keeping context.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the destruction as happening in this moment.
Do not show creation, Adam, or the tower events as present scenes.

title: Ether’s ancestry begins
summary: Moroni gives the account, identifies Ether as the record writer and a descendant of Coriantor, and recounts the lineage from Coriantor through Shiblon.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni is the first-person narrator giving the account.
Ether wrote the record and was a descendant of Coriantor.
Coriantor was the son of Moron.
Moron was the son of Ethem.
Ethem was the son of Ahah.
Ahah was the son of Seth.
Seth was the son of Shiblon.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A simple lineage or record-page visual may accompany Moroni’s narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and appearances of the named ancestors are not described.

narration.text: And on this wise do I give the account.
He that wrote this record was Ether, and he was a descendant of Coriantor.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The “I” in the opening narration is Moroni, not Ether.
The ancestry is reported, not presented as an event occurring alongside Moroni.
prohibited_inventions: Do not quote the suggested wording “And now I, Moroni, proceed to give an account”; it is not in the supplied verses.
Do not portray the ancestors together or imply they are physically present with Moroni.

title: The lineage continues

explicit_facts.text: Shiblon was Com’s son; Com was Coriantum’s son; Coriantum was Amnigaddah’s son; Amnigaddah was Aaron’s son; Aaron was a descendant of Heth, who was Hearthom’s son; and Hearthom was Lib’s son.

explicit_facts.text: Lib was Kish’s son; Kish was Corom’s son; Corom was Levi’s son; Levi was Kim’s son; Kim was Morianton’s son; and Morianton was a descendant of Riplakish.

explicit_facts.text: Omer was Shule’s son; Shule was Kib’s son; Kib was Orihah’s son; and Orihah was Jared’s son.

title: Jared’s people leave the tower

title: Jared asks his brother to pray
summary: Jared asks his brother to cry unto the Lord so they will not be confounded; his brother does so, and the Lord has compassion upon Jared, preserving their language.

explicit_facts.text: The brother of Jared was large and mighty and highly favored of the Lord.
Jared asked his brother to cry unto the Lord so they would not be confounded.
The brother of Jared cried unto the Lord; the Lord had compassion upon Jared and did not confound Jared’s language, and the brothers were not confounded.

title: The promised journey and nation
summary: The Lord tells the brother of Jared to lead the others into a northward valley after completing an earlier task. He promises to meet him, go before him into a choice land, bless him and his seed, and raise up a great nation from his seed, his brother’s seed, and those who go with him. He says this is because they have cried unto him for a long time.

explicit_facts.text: After the brother of Jared has done the task referred to as “this,” he is to go at the head of the others into the northward valley.
The Lord promises to meet him there and go before him into a land described as choice above all the lands of the earth.
The Lord promises to bless him and his seed and to raise up a great nation from his seed, his brother’s seed, and those who go with him.
The Lord says he will do this because they have cried unto him for a long time.
